jobs.excerpt: Senior Data Analyst IIWould you like to be part of a team that delivers high-quality Analytics to our customers?
jobs.description:
Senior Data Analyst II

Would you like to be part of a team that delivers high-quality Analytics to our customers?

Are you a highly visible champion with a ‘can do’ attitude and enthusiasm that inspires others?


About our Team:-

Our team turns operational data into insight. By measuring and improving how content is created, validated, and delivered across Health Content Management, Data Operations, and Journals Operations, we cut turnaround times, raise quality, and give stakeholders clear visibility into performance. Every efficiency we unlock helps Elsevier deliver trusted, evidence-based content that supports providers, prepares students, improves clinical outcomes, and benefits every patient.


About the Role:-

The Senior Data Analyst II takes ownership of analysis and reporting from the first question to the final result. The work helps content move through our operations faster and more smoothly, supports better decisions based on facts, and speeds up ongoing improvement across our global teams. The role works with a high degree of independence: it turns loosely defined business questions into clear ideas to test, builds the right tools to answer them (dashboards, performance measures, and in-depth studies), and guides senior stakeholders with clear, story-driven insights. Experience in publishing is helpful but not required. What matters is a willingness to learn, or a strong existing grasp of, how content travels from start to finish and where it is handed from one team to another. This includes how content and its connected data are created and managed, where suppliers get involved, the steps in each workflow, the quality checks along the way, the points where work goes wrong or has to be redone, and the factors that drive volume and speed.

The role works closely with operations leaders and neighboring teams, such as strategy, content production, finance, the central analytics group, and technology and data teams. Together they make sure everyone measures success in the same way, relies on trustworthy data, and sees real, measurable improvements in how work gets done.


A Senior Data Analyst II is a recognized expert in their area. They increasingly influence not only what is reported, but also how the organization thinks about measurement, quality, and performance. They coach junior analysts and help business users read and use reports correctly and consistently.

Responsibilities:-


1. Stakeholder Partnership and Insight Leadership

  • Lead analytics engagements independently, from clarifying objectives and framing hypotheses to defining success measures and executing end-to-end.
  • Act as a thought partner to senior stakeholders: priorities meaningful metrics, offer options, trade-offs, impact sizing and monitoring plans.
  • Proactively surface problem areas in the content journey (bottlenecks, defect leakage, rework, delays, supplier variability, workload imbalance) and propose targeted analyses and actions.
  • Present recommendations as clear, non-technical narratives tailored to stakeholder context and decision points.

2. Reporting, Dashboards and KPI Delivery

  • Deliver reports, dashboards and BI structures that meet business requirements and support trend and performance analysis.
  • Define best-fit reporting: KPI definitions and levels (team to global), metric logic, segmentation, benchmarking and an adoption plan to embed usage in BAU.
  • Deliver accurate, timely KPI reporting at every stakeholder level; partner with Data Management to publish trusted dashboards with consistent definitions and strong quality controls.

3. Publishing Domain and Content-Flow Process Analytics

  • Apply deep knowledge of publishing and content operations to interpret workflow behavior and find improvement opportunities.
  • Build measurement frameworks covering throughput and cycle time (lead, queue and touch time), stage-level performance and handoff quality, rework and defect drivers, supplier variation and risk hotspots, and productivity, capacity and workload distribution.
  • Work with process owners to turn operational pain points into measurable indicators and actionable improvement levers.

4. Data Preparation, Integration and Engineering Literacy

  • Handle large, complex datasets and combine multiple sources using SQL and modern analytics tooling.
  • Understand integration mechanics: pipelines, transformations, joins, grain, lineage, refresh cadence and performance constraints.
  • Work with big data platforms (Databricks preferred); SQL essential; Python and/or Scala desirable; KNIME, Tableau/Power BI and Snowflake exposure an advantage.
  • Bridge business needs and technical implementation so solutions are scalable, maintainable and aligned to platform standards.

5. Advanced Analytics, Modelling and Statistical Thinking

  • Apply techniques suited to the problem: trend decomposition, segmentation, cohort analysis, anomaly detection, hypothesis testing, correlation exploration and scenario modelling.
  • Develop predictive analytics, basic machine learning and NLP use cases where relevant, and translate outputs into operational recommendations, guardrails and monitoring metrics, not just model accuracy.

6. Data Governance, Quality and Metric Consistency

  • Safeguard quality, integrity, completeness, timeliness and reliability; run regular data quality assessments and resolve gaps and discrepancies.
  • Align metric definitions across teams to remove inconsistencies between dashboards; lead or co-lead documentation (definitions, KPI logic, change logs, refresh schedules, known limitations).
  • Champion a data quality culture in which data trust is foundational to performance management.

7. Coaching, Enablement and Community Leadership

  • Coach junior analysts on data preparation, modelling, visualisation standards, stakeholder management and project execution.
  • Train and support reporting champions and business users for consistent, effective use of reports; promote problem resolution and best-practice adoption among fellow analysts.

8. Project and Program Contribution

  • Lead medium/tactical analytics projects with minimal oversight, managing tasks, blockers, timelines and expectations.
  • Join international programs needing analytics/BI expertise: set metrics to monitor success criteria, support planning and resourcing with analysis and documentation, and automate wherever feasible.
  • Represent the analytics function in governance discussions and communicate decisions to the wider reporting community.

Requirements:-

Education: Bachelor's degree required, with preference for a quantitative discipline (Economics, Math, Statistics, Data Science, Engineering or similar); Master's/PhD a plus, particularly for modelling-heavy work.

Experience: Typically 8+ years in data or business analytics, ideally in a global multinational; preference for exposure to publishing operations, content-flow or equivalent process-heavy domains.

Essential skills: Requirements gathering and stakeholder management; advanced analytical skills with attention to detail; strong SQL on large datasets; high proficiency in Tableau and/or Power BI; excellent communication and decision-oriented data storytelling for non-technical audiences; strong documentation discipline.

Desirable skills: Databricks; Python and/or Scala (not essential); statistical modelling; Snowflake; KNIME or similar tooling; familiarity with data warehousing and modern analytics architectures.

Functional Competencies (Expected Level)

  • Thought Partnership: Guides stakeholders through hypothesis-led thinking, selects the most relevant analyses and metrics, and helps set goals aligned to business objectives.
  • Data Preparation: Expert at blending data across tools and big data platforms; coaches others.
  • Data Modelling: Applies advanced scenarios and statistical approaches to big datasets; coaches modelling techniques.
  • Data Visualisation: Designs user-centric dashboards and influences stakeholders through high-impact communication.
  • Data-Driven Culture: Identifies barriers and opportunities, proposes practical solutions, and influences beyond the analytics team.
  • Domain Skills: Advanced understanding of content-flow and publishing operations; builds working knowledge of adjacent domains.
  • Project Management: Leads medium/tactical projects, resolves blockers, assigns work effectively and coaches juniors.

Behaviours (Advancing Leader | Professional Individual Contributor)

  • Collaborate to Deliver: Enable winning teams through collaboration and constructive challenge; coach and develop talent; communicate with clarity; lead inclusively and minimise bias.
  • Drive Commercial Edge: Act strategically and anticipate future needs; prioritise customers using data; value data through benchmarks and accuracy checks; deliver sustainable performance with ownership.
  • Act with Agility: Think enterprise-wide and cross-RELX; stay curious about new tools and techniques; navigate ambiguity with considered, calculated decisions; build networks across cultures and geographies.

What Success Looks Like

  • Stakeholders consistently use dashboards and insights to run performance conversations and drive action.
  • Content-flow bottlenecks and quality pain points are quantified, explained and improved through measurable interventions.
  • KPI definitions and reporting logic are consistent across teams, and data trust improves through governance and documentation.
  • Junior analysts and reporting champions grow through structured coaching and enablement.

Analytics delivery becomes faster, more scalable and more embedded in BAU operations

Do you want to empower organizations to build smarter compensation strategies while ensuring fair pay for all employees?

Syndio is the leading pay governance and compensation intelligence platform. We help organizations make better pay decisions at every stage of the compensation lifecycle, from leveling and offers to promotions and merit. Our platform gives HR, compensation, and finance leaders the data and decision support they need to govern pay fairly, compliantly, and with confidence. We partner with many of the world’s most recognized and respected enterprises, helping them implement leading-edge compensation solutions with expert guidance and analyzing pay for over 10 million employees across the world.

Join us in our mission to help companies make smarter pay decisions they can trust!

About the role

Syndio is the platform more than half the Fortune 100 trust to govern pay decisions, built on a decade of pay equity work and millions of pay records. Executive Engagement & Insights is the team that turns that into research, category leadership, and executive-level experiences elevating pay to a strategic decision rather than a compliance afterthought.

A CHRO or CFO decides to buy our platform once. Inspiring them to feel personally invested in what we’re enabling for their business takes something special, and that is what separates a vendor from a valued business partner. This role exists to help build that.

We're hiring a Director of Executive Engagement to own three things. The first is our Strategic Advisors program, along with an expansion launching later in 2026. You'll onboard advisors, keep them genuinely engaged, and nurture those relationships into outside credibility, introductions that open doors, and sharper strategic thinking. The second is the experience we create for executives among our customers. Working sessions, private briefings, peer roundtables, and executive forum programming that earns time from people who guard it closely and inspire leadership action related to pay governance. The third is our relationships with industry analysts, keeping them informed on Syndio and tapping into their expertise and insights.

You'll report to our SVP of Executive Engagement & Insights and work regularly with our CEO, and the senior leadership team. You'll also work closely with Marketing, Sales, and Product to connect them with customer executives, advisors, and analysts in ways that expand opportunities for the business and drive revenue.

Why this job is exciting

  • Build the advisor bench. Identify who we need, drive recruiting efforts, and design a sustainable rhythm that keeps senior executives willing to contribute year after year.
  • Design what executives remember. Create and continually refine working sessions, briefings, and executive forum programming that changes how a leader thinks about pay.
  • Turn access into revenue. Match the right executive to the right moment with Marketing and Sales, and get senior leaders invested before there's a deal on the table.
  • Influence at the highest levels. Build relationships with exceptional senior leaders and work directly with Syndio’s senior leadership team.
  • Sharpen how we see the market. Industry analysts talk with buyers and vendors all day. You’ll bring what they see back to our leadership team and help influence our plans around it.

About you

  • A track record working with senior executives at multi-national enterprises. You've earned time from people who guard it, and held onto it well beyond a single meeting.
  • A record of relationships that produced business outcomes. Intros that became pipeline, advisors who influenced a decision, execs who became advocates. You can point to what came of them.
  • Strong design instinct. You've built executive experiences and programming content from scratch. While you sweat the details of the room, you always measure the work by the specific value a leader walks away with.
  • Influence without authority. You'll partner closely with Marketing and work across Go-to-Market functions and the company leadership team.

Some travel comes with this role and may grow as the programs do.

Nice to have

  • Experience running an advisory board, council, or similar program of external experts.
  • Facilitation skills. You can run the room yourself when that's the right call.
  • Familiarity with how enterprise sales cycles work and where exec relationships help move them.
  • Familiarity with industry analyst firms and how they work with vendors.
  • Domain knowledge in compensation, total rewards, people analytics, or the finance side of workforce planning.

Why you'll love it here:

  • 💰 Competitive Compensation. For this role our salary is targeted at $182,000 -$215,000 per year. Final offer amounts are determined by factors such as experience and expertise. We take a geo neutral approach to compensation within the US, meaning that we pay based on job function and level, not location.
  • 🏆 Syndio Equity. So you can share in Syndio’s success.
  • 🏝 Flexible Vacation Policy. We encourage our team to recharge when they need to, plus paid sick & safe time, compassion leave, and voting leave.
  • Paid parental leave
  • 🩺 Medical, Dental, Vision. Syndio pays 90% of employee premiums, and 50% for dependents.
  • 🏥 Life Insurance & Disability. Syndio covers the full premium.
  • 🏦 401(k). To help you save for your future
  • Fully remote model -

The interview overview

Below you'll find an outline of the interview plan for our Director position. Please note that this is what we expect the process to look like; we may ask you for supplemental information or require an additional step before making a final decision.

  • 30 minute interview with a member of our Talent Team
  • 45 minute Zoom interview with the Hiring Manager

If you share these values and are interested in joining us, we'd love to talk with you even if you don't 100% meet the "about you" listed here. With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 31,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

Employee Contract Type:

Local - Fixed Term Employee (Fixed Term)

Job Description:

JOB PURPOSE

Provide strategic and technical leadership to advance gender equality, disability inclusion and social inclusion across the East Asia region. The role develops and delivers a regional GEDSI roadmap; strengthens organisational practice and staff and partner capability; embeds GEDSI across strategy, programme and proposal design, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning; and positions World Vision with donors, governments, UN agencies, civil society and representative organisations.


Core Areas of Focus

  • Develop and execute an East Asia regional GEDSI strategy and roadmap aligned with organisational policy and child well-being priorities.
  • Lead GEDSI mainstreaming and quality assurance across regional and national office programming, grants and organisational systems.
  • Build the capability of GEDSI focal points, technical teams, leaders, partners and representative organisations.
  • Generate evidence, learning, innovation and external positioning on GEDSI across development, humanitarian and fragile contexts.
  • Manage and coordinate GEDSI-related consultancies, technical assistance engagements, and partnerships, including development of scopes of work, procurement inputs, quality assurance, delivery oversight, and dissemination of outputs to ensure alignment with global and regional priorities and standards.

KEY RESPONSIBILITES

Lead regional GEDSI strategy, policy implementation and organizational change.

  • Develop and monitor a regional GEDSI strategy and roadmap aligned with organizational priorities and policy.
  • Engage regional and national leadership, People & Culture, operations, programmes, grants, advocacy and communications to embed GEDSI in programming, organizational practices, advocacy and external engagement, and in communications, as per World Vision’s GEDSI Policy.
  • Guide organizational GEDSI self-assessments and action plans; promote inclusive language, accessible workplaces, non-discrimination and reasonable accommodation.
  • Ensure GEDSI is visible in organizational priorities, program strategies and design, key messages and resource allocation.

Lead GEDSI mainstreaming in programs, implementation and proposals across funding streams.

  • Provide technical leadership for GEDSI-responsive and transformative programme and proposal design across sectors and contexts.
  • Ensure designs are informed by GEDSI analysis, including gender and disability analysis, barriers, disparities, harmful norms, root causes and intersectional risks.
  • Advise teams on GEDSI objectives, theories of change, indicators, budgets, risk mitigation, Do No Harm, safeguarding and donor requirements.
  • Contextualize and promote GEDSI tools, approaches, minimum standards, domains of change, continuum and marker.
  • Strengthen identification and use of disaggregated data, including appropriate use of Washington Group Questions or other approved tools, informing program / project designs based on analysis.
  • Coach teams to monitor emerging barriers and adapt implementation to improve equitable access, participation, decision-making, systems and well-being.
  • Promote rights-based and social-model approaches that address attitudinal, environmental, communication and institutional barriers.
  • Develop, manage, monitor, and communicate progress on the Disability Consultant’s workplan and project deliverables, ensuring alignment with EAS GEDSI priorities and agreed objectives.

Build GEDSI capability, networks and communities of practice.

  • Assess competency and capacity gaps and develop regional capacity-strengthening plans for staff, focal points, partners and leaders.
  • Deliver and coordinate contextualised training, coaching, mentoring and peer learning on gender equality, disability inclusion, social inclusion and related frameworks.
  • Empower GEDSI focal points and technical teams with tools, models, resources and quality-assurance support.
  • Strengthen regional collaboration networks and communities of practice, including linkages with gender equality and disability inclusion leadership networks.

Lead evidence, learning, innovation and knowledge management.

  • Develop and implement a regional GEDSI learning agenda linked to child well-being outcomes.
  • Initiate and oversee research, pilots and testing of new or adapted GEDSI approaches and programming models.
  • Support analysis and use of data, evaluations, learning reviews, impact stories, case studies and promising practices.
  • Facilitate knowledge sharing across national offices, the wider Partnership and external audiences.

Build strategic partnerships, external positioning and thought leadership.

  • Represent and position World Vision with governments, donors, UN agencies, clusters, working groups, NGOs, faith actors, academia and regional networks.
  • Build or increase capacity to build strategic and equitable partnerships with women-led organizations, organizations of persons with disabilities and minority groups as part of social inclusion, including children, to ensure that they participate meaningfully in assessment, design, implementation, monitoring, learning and advocacy.
  • Identify opportunities for shared learning, advocacy, policy influence, resource mobilization and thought leadership.
  • Support communications and external engagement colleagues to use inclusive, rights-based and evidence-informed GEDSI language and narratives.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILL AND EXPERIENCE

  • A bachelor’s degree with substantial relevant experience may be considered.
  • Relevant professional development in gender equality, disability inclusion, social inclusion, safeguarding, programme design, MEAL or humanitarian programming.
  • Minimum 5 years of demonstrated experience providing strategic and technical leadership on gender equality, disability inclusion and social inclusion in international development and/or humanitarian programming.
  • Experience supporting GEDSI-responsive and transformative designs, mainstreaming strategies and activities across multiple sectors and funding streams.
  • Experience leading GEDSI analysis, including gender and disability analysis, and integrating findings into design, implementation, monitoring, evaluation and learning.
  • Strong facilitation, coaching, relationship-building, partnership, influencing, writing and presentation skills.
  • Experience working in or across the East Asia region and adapting global approaches to diverse national and local contexts.
  • Substantial experience in disability-inclusive programming, accessibility, disability-disaggregated data, partnership with organisations of persons with disabilities, and rights-based approaches.
  • Experience in organisational change, policy implementation, advocacy, research, knowledge management, external engagement and donor positioning.
  • Experience leading or supporting organisational GEDSI self-assessments, audits or action plans and building the capability of staff and partners.
  • Experience applying Do No Harm, safeguarding and ethical approaches to gender-based violence and other GEDSI-related risks.

Required Language(s):

  • English, both written and verbal

Required travel and/or work environment accommodations:

  • The position requires approximately 20% travel, subject to field office needs.
  • The successful candidate will be based in their home country and will work remotely, with travel to field locations, regional offices, and partner meetings as required.

Preferred Experience, Knowledge and/or other Qualifications

  • Master’s degree or equivalent in gender studies, disability studies, social or political sciences, social work, international development, economics, public policy, programme management or a related field.
  • Detailed knowledge of current gender equality, disability inclusion and broader social inclusion approaches in development, humanitarian and fragile contexts.
  • Knowledge of the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, CEDAW, the Convention on the Rights of the Child and relevant donor frameworks and markers.
  • Ability to connect GEDSI programming and organisational change to child well-being outcomes.
  • Ability to analyse and communicate disaggregated evidence, identify barriers and root causes, and translate findings into practical programme, policy and budget recommendations.
  • Experience with World Vision or another faith-based organisation and ability to articulate faith-based foundations for equality, dignity and inclusion in a contextually appropriate way.
  • Knowledge of organisational GEDSI policies, GEDSI domains of change, continuum and marker, inclusive accountability mechanisms and recognised disability data tools.
  • Experience piloting and scaling contextualised, locally led GEDSI programming models and working with representative organisations.

jobs.title: Transmission Line Engineer II/ III- High Voltage
jobs.excerpt: Role SummaryAs a Transmission Line Engineer II/III, you will design the overhead high- and medium-voltage lines that connect utility-scale solar and battery storage projects to the grid.
jobs.description:
Role Summary

As a Transmission Line Engineer II/III, you will design the overhead high- and medium-voltage lines that connect utility-scale solar and battery storage projects to the grid. A gen-tie line is often the last link between a finished plant and the energy it delivers, and your work decides whether that link is safe, buildable, and cost-effective. You will turn project requirements into construction-ready designs, working alongside substation, protection and controls, and civil engineers on the High Voltage team. The work you produce will directly support the addition of utility-scale renewable energy generation assets to the power grid.

As an employee-owner, you will share in the results of the work and help build a team where every engineer’s contribution is recognized. Candidates may be considered at either the Engineer II or Engineer III level depending on experience, technical depth, independence, and demonstrated ability to lead scope.

Duties & Responsibilities

Across both levels, this role may include:

Core Technical & Functional Responsibilities

  • Design overhead gen-tie, transmission, and medium-voltage lines in PLS-CADD, including route evaluation, plan and profile development, structure spotting, sag-tension analysis, conductor selection, and clearance verification.
  • Model and check wood, steel, and concrete pole structures and lattice towers in PLS-POLE and PLS-TOWER under the governing load cases.
  • Prepare structure load sheets and specifications for custom steel poles, and review fabricator drawings for conformance with the design.
  • Develop insulator and hardware assemblies, framing details, and bills of material.
  • Design or coordinate direct-embed and drilled pier foundations using geotechnical reports and foundation design software.
  • Build terrain models and crossing data from LiDAR and survey files for use in line design.
  • Produce development, permitting, and issued-for-construction drawing and specification packages.
  • Contribute to substation steel structure, bus support, and general arrangement deliverables with the substation physical design team, where your experience allows.
  • Adapt standard design methods to non-routine conditions such as road, rail, and line crossings, constrained right-of-way, and long spans, and bring unconventional problems to senior engineers for review.

Project & Portfolio Execution

  • Lead small transmission line projects, or defined portions of larger ones, from kickoff through issued-for-construction.
  • Manage assigned design scopes to schedule and budget, and report progress and risks to the project lead.
  • Track RFIs, design changes, and scope changes, and update deliverables when project inputs change.
  • Support construction by answering contractor questions, reviewing field changes, and preparing record drawings.

Quality, Standards & Compliance

  • Ensure designs meet NESC, ASCE 74, ASCE 48, IEEE, and applicable utility and jurisdictional requirements.
  • Follow Revamp QA/QC procedures, self-check models and calculations, and resolve review comments before issue.
  • Document design criteria, assumptions, and load cases so reviewers and clients can verify the basis of design.

Collaboration & Communication

  • Coordinate with substation physical, protection and controls, and civil engineers on line terminations, dead-end structures, and access roads.
  • Work with surveyors, geotechnical consultants, and right-of-way teams to resolve alignment and structure placement conflicts.
  • Attend project meetings and present line design progress, open issues, and recommendations.

Additional Expectations at the Engineer III Level

  • Lead multiple transmission line projects at once, preparing and owning scope, schedule, and budget.
  • Select design criteria and solve complex design problems independently, seeking guidance only on unconventional conditions.
  • Support client interaction for multiple projects in a portfolio, including design reviews and technical clarifications.
  • Develop work plans and assign tasks to discipline team members.
  • Mentor Engineer I and II staff and review their models, calculations, and drawings.
  • Act as Engineer of Record on line design packages when licensed and assigned.

Additional Responsibilities

  • Perform essential duties including meeting deliverables and deadlines.
  • Perform additional related duties as assigned or directed.

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Civil, Structural, Electrical, or Mechanical Engineering, or a closely related engineering field.
  • Overhead transmission or distribution line design experience: typically 2+ years for Engineer II and 5+ years for Engineer III.
  • Working proficiency in PLS-CADD, including sag-tension analysis, structure spotting, and clearance checks.
  • Experience modeling structures in PLS-POLE or PLS-TOWER.
  • Working knowledge of NESC, ASCE 74, and ASCE 48 as they apply to overhead line design.
  • Experience preparing plan and profile drawings, structure load sheets, and material lists.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, including documenting calculations for review.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Engineer in Training (EIT) certification or Professional Engineer (PE) license.
  • Experience designing gen-tie lines for utility-scale solar, storage, or other generation interconnections.
  • Foundation design experience with PLS-CAISSON or MFAD.
  • Experience processing LiDAR data for line design.
  • Proficiency with AutoCAD or MicroStation.
  • Substation physical or substation steel design experience (steel structures, bus supports, general arrangements), or exposure to underground transmission design.

Benefits for Full-Time Positions

  • Participation in Revamp's Employee Ownership ESOP program.

•Competitive compensation with bonus.

  • Full benefits package offerings including 99% employer-paid health, vision, life, and dental insurance.
  • Medical, dependent care, and commuter FSA.

•Monthly health and wellness stipend.

  • Attractive vacation, sick, and holiday pay.

•Paid parental leave.

  • 401(k) savings plan with 100% match up to 6%, vested immediately.
  • Paid volunteer time off and charitable donation matching.

About Revamp

Founded in 2016, Revamp is the premier employee-owned engineering design firm dedicated to advancing large-scale renewable energy projects. Our team is united by a shared commitment to accelerating the global energy transition and creating a workplace where talented people can make a tangible impact in the fight against climate change.

As employee-owners, we take pride in building a culture of collaboration, innovation, and accountability where every individual's contribution drives both company success and personal growth. Revamp engineers have supported the design of more than 10% of the utility-scale solar generation capacity in the US since 2020, contributing directly to the renewable energy transformation.

So much more than just an engineering firm; we are a diverse, international team of artists, singers, dancers, pastry chefs, outdoor enthusiasts, animal lovers, travelers and problem-solvers who bring curiosity and creativity to everything we do. For more information, visit www.revamp‑eng.com.

Disclaimers

Employment with Revamp Engineering Inc. may be subject to background checks that are permitted by applicable law and relevant to the position. Any such checks will be conducted in compliance with all legal requirements, including providing notice, obtaining consent where required, and allowing candidates to access and correct personal information as permitted by law.

Revamp Engineering Inc. is an equal opportunity employer committed to creating an inclusive workplace. We provide equal employment opportunities without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law. We value diversity and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply. Revamp Engineering Inc. is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities. If you require an accommodation during the application or interview process, please contact us.

It compares the information you submit (your resume or CV and your answers to application questions) against criteria our recruiting team sets for the role. Nuestros DaCoders tienen un impacto significativo en el éxito de nuestro negocio y el de nuestros clientes. Serás la persona experta participando en nuestros proyectos, con acceso a startups disruptivas y marcas globales.

¿Te interesa?

Sobre el rol

Buscamos un/a Machine Learning Engineer Semi-Senior o Senior para sumarse, a través de DaCodes bajo un esquema de staff augmentation, al equipo de IA/ML de una startup de ad-tech con base en Argentina y operación 100% remota, enfocada en construir una capa de infraestructura de nueva generación para la monetización inteligente de apps móviles. Esta plataforma funciona como un “control plane” de monetización: se integra sobre las plataformas de mediación que ya usan las apps (como AppLovin MAX, Unity LevelPlay y AdMob) y coordina en tiempo real fuentes de demanda, cohortes de usuarios, placements y reglas de monetización.

El foco principal del rol está en machine learning: modelos que predicen comportamiento de usuarios y del mercado publicitario, y que actúan sobre esas predicciones en tiempo real. También colaborarás en iniciativas de IA generativa, como un agente LLM que ayuda al equipo de operaciones publicitarias y a los clientes a operar su monetización.

Buscamos un perfil proactivo, que se adapte bien a un entorno poco jerárquico y con requerimientos no siempre perfectamente estructurados.

  • Colaborar en iniciativas de IA generativa, incluyendo integraciones con APIs internas de analytics y configuración, sets de evaluación, observabilidad y controles human-in-the-loop.
  • Contribuir al desarrollo de software asistido por IA, construyendo herramientas y contexto para que los coding agents trabajen de forma efectiva sobre el código base.

Requirements

  • Dominio de Python y SQL, incluyendo el stack científico de Python (pandas o Polars, scikit-learn).
  • Experiencia con distintos tipos de modelos (clasificación, regresión, ranking) y criterio para elegir el más adecuado según el problema.
  • Base sólida en estadística: calibración de probabilidades, clasificación desbalanceada, métricas de evaluación más allá del accuracy, y A/B testing.
  • Experiencia práctica trabajando con LLMs: tool calling, diseño de prompts, evaluación de outputs de agentes, y uso de coding agents en el día a día.
  • Familiaridad con plataformas de datos, particularmente Spark/Databricks, Airflow y AWS.
  • Capacidad de resolución de problemas y troubleshooting de modelos y datos en producción.

About the Team

DoorDash’s mission is to grow and empower local economies. By building intelligent, last-mile delivery technology for local cities, DoorDash connects people with the local businesses they care about, helping grow businesses and the communities that support those businesses.

Our Consumer Retention Marketing team is responsible for building lasting relationships with our customers through personalized, scalable, cross-channel experiences that drive engagement and long-term value. We focus on connecting consumers with the most relevant products, merchants, and moments across DoorDash’s expanding ecosystem, including New Verticals like Grocery, Convenience, Alcohol, and Retail, as well as high-impact seasonal and cultural Occasions.

About the Role

As the Assoc Manager of Customer Lifecycle Marketing for USMP New, you will own DoorDash's new consumer onboarding lifecycle — the programs, channels, and experiences that take a customer from the moment they sign up to the point where DoorDash is a habitual part of their life.

This is a high-investment, high-impact area. You will not just maintain what exists — you will push it forward. That means aggressively iterating on core onboarding programs, expanding the surfaces through which we reach new consumers, introducing personalization based on customer behavior and context, and managing a meaningful budget across channels. You will move quickly, test often, and build toward an onboarding system that is more intelligent, more multi-surface, and more effective at converting new signups into long-term engaged customers.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives on end-to-end program ownership, is energized by improving conversion through both creative and analytical thinking, and wants to build something they can point to and say — I made this meaningfully better.

  • Own the new consumer onboarding strategy — define the full lifecycle from sign-up through habituation, including key milestones, trigger logic, channel sequencing, and success metrics

  • 7+ years of direct people management or practice leadership experience overseeing business analysis teams.

  • Proven background standardizing BA methodologies, establishing knowledge management practices, and managing resource capacity across concurrent projects.

About RemotePass

RemotePass is a leading global platform transforming how businesses access and manage top talent. Recognised as one of G2's Top 100 Fastest Growing Software Products, we're breaking down geographical barriers so exceptional talent can thrive anywhere.

By streamlining global hiring, onboarding, payroll, and compliance, RemotePass helps organisations build high-performing remote teams and gives workers worldwide unprecedented access to global employers.

We're backed by world-class investors: Endeavor Catalyst, Khwarizmi Ventures, Oraseya Capital, Flyer One Ventures, Access Bridge Ventures, A15, Swiss Founders Fund and Plug & Play.

About the Role

RemotePass is expanding into new markets worldwide, and this role sits at the heart of that growth. You'll own establishing new RemotePass entities and keeping existing ones in good standing.

It's a hands-on, delivery-focused role for a natural go-getter who gets things over the line. For each new market, you'll work with a small cross-functional team spanning legal, finance, and operations, driving the work from scoping through to a fully operational entity. You'll project-manage every stage and work closely with senior stakeholders, including our CEO. Once an entity is live, you'll ensure a clean handover to the operational team and oversee ongoing renewals.

You don't need to be a qualified lawyer, but you should be comfortable operating in a legal and compliance environment, understand what incorporation and licensing involves, and finding efficient ways to get the work done.

The role offers real scope to grow, with opportunities to contribute to wider legal, compliance, and operations initiatives as your remit develops.

What You'll Do

  • Manage our global entity lifecycle. Own entity setup and maintenance globally, from market scoping through corporate governance, statutory compliance, and restructuring where needed. Direct a cross-functional team across legal, finance, and operations, owning the plan and delivery at every stage.
  • Engage senior stakeholders. Keep leadership (including the CEO), internal teams, and external partners aligned through clear progress reporting. Surface risks early and drive decisions to keep projects moving.
  • Navigate governance and regulatory requirements. Manage incorporation, licensing, notarisation, certification, legalisation, employer registrations, licence renewals, statutory filings, and local regulatory obligations, finding the most efficient routes at scale-up pace.
  • Keep entities compliant. Maintain corporate records and manage renewals, registrations, filings, director/shareholder changes, board and shareholder resolutions, POAs, UBO updates, and registered office requirements. Ensure each entity stays in good standing and transitions smoothly to business-as-usual.
  • Broaden your impact. Contribute to vendor and corporate legal matters: NDAs, vendor agreements, banking documentation, lease agreements, procurement reviews, contract templates, legal playbooks, and legal ops improvements more broadly.

Requirements

What We're Looking For

  • 4 to 6 years in company secretarial, corporate governance, entity management, or paralegal work, ideally at a corporate service provider, incorporation specialist, or a larger company's corporate affairs or legal function (must have).
  • Hands-on ownership of corporate records, statutory filings, and board and shareholder resolutions across multiple entities, including drafting resolutions independently, not just filing them (must have).
  • Experience supporting a multi-entity or multinational group across jurisdictions (must have).
  • Strong project management, keeping multiple workstreams, providers, and stakeholders on track at once.
  • Excellent communication, credible with senior leaders and external partners.
  • Familiar with notarisation, certification, and legalisation of corporate documents.
  • Proactive, detail-oriented, and comfortable in a fully remote, fast-moving scale-up.
  • Fluent in English.

You'll Thrive in This Role If

  • You like owning a process start to finish and making sure it lands.
  • You're energised by leading cross-functional teams and partners toward a clear outcome.
  • You're confident engaging senior stakeholders and communicating progress clearly.
  • You spot problems before they become issues.
  • You want broad responsibility and room to grow your remit.

Benefits

Why Join RemotePass?

  • Play a central role in RemotePass's international expansion.
  • Take genuine end-to-end ownership of a high-impact function.
  • Get regular exposure to senior leadership and room to broaden your remit.
  • Work in a collaborative, ownership-driven culture.
  • Competitive compensation and benefits, with real growth opportunities.

jobs.description:
Your Future Evolves Here

Evolent partners with health plans and providers to achieve better outcomes for people with most complex and costly health conditions. Working across specialties and primary care, we seek to connect the pieces of fragmented health care system and ensure people get the same level of care and compassion we would want for our loved ones.

Evolent employees enjoy work/life balance, the flexibility to suit their work to their lives, and autonomy they need to get things done. We believe that people do their best work when they're supported to live their best lives, and when they feel welcome to bring their whole selves to work. That's one reason why diversity and inclusion are core to our business.

Join Evolent for the mission. Stay for the culture.

What You’ll Be Doing:

Position Summary

The Senior QA Automation Engineer leads the quality strategy for the Evolent Platform web user experience. This role designs and maintains end-to-end, component, accessibility, contract, and test automation for a React and Next.js application and owns the quality signals that determine release readiness.

This individual works independently with minimal supervision, applies creativity to testing challenges, sets and upholds the automation patterns others follow, and mentors quality engineers across the team. The role is expected to use approved AI-assisted tools to accelerate testing and improve quality while remaining fully accountable for every delivered result.

AI-Assisted Engineering Expectations

Evolent engineers are expected to effectively leverage approved AI-assisted development and productivity tools (e.g., code assistants, copilots, automation agents, knowledge assistants, and analytics tools) to improve quality, efficiency, and innovation while maintaining accountability for all delivered work. These expectations span the full engineering lifecycle, not only code generation, including iterating with AI on test strategy and solution design, evaluating alternatives, and producing design artifacts. Engineers remain responsible for validating outputs, ensuring solution quality, protecting sensitive information, and complying with security, privacy, regulatory, and Responsible AI standards.

Key Responsibilities

Quality Strategy and Leadership

  • Develop, implement, and manage comprehensive test strategies for the user experience, covering functional, regression, accessibility, performance, and AI-output quality.
  • Participate in code reviews, design discussions, and product planning to ensure quality is built into all phases of the software lifecycle.
  • Define and uphold test automation patterns and standards in partnership with testing automation architects and front-end leads.
  • Mentor quality engineers, promoting best practices in testing, automation, and quality assurance.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives in testing processes, tools, and methodologies, and evaluate emerging testing technologies for applicability.

Test Automation and CI/CD

  • Lead the creation, maintenance, and optimization of Playwright end-to-end suites and Vitest component tests for React and Next.js features.
  • Build contract tests for the AG-UI event stream, verifying event sequencing, shared state, tool-call events, and human-in-the-loop approval interrupts.
  • Build API tests for backend-for-frontend endpoints and .NET and Python (FastAPI) services.
  • Test streaming behavior and resilience, including slow, interrupted, and failed agent calls, retries, and timeouts.
  • Plan and execute basic load and performance tests for streaming endpoints and data-heavy screens.
  • Integrate and execute automated suites in GitHub Actions, maintaining a consistently high pass rate and reliable results.

Accessibility Testing

  • Lead accessibility testing against WCAG 2.1/2.2 AA and Section 508, combining automated axe-core checks with manual screen reader testing using JAWS, NVDA, and VoiceOver.
  • Partner with engineering and design to triage accessibility defects and support independent accessibility conformance reviews.

Defect Management and Quality Reporting

  • Isolate, analyze, document, and prioritize defects before escalating to developers, and collaborate with developers, business analysts, and stakeholders for timely resolution.
  • Analyze test and evaluation results, generate quality metrics, and report on quality state and release readiness to stakeholders.

jobs.description:
Job Description:

Job Summary

The Principal Engineer, AI Orchestration & Retrieval defines how the enterprise's central AI system is composed – the orchestration and abstraction layers that connect LLMs to tools, data, and one another, and the retrieval systems that ground them. This role sets the strategy and builds the reality for how we build and expose tools (including MCP servers), how we structure retrieval and chunking, and when to rely on specialized sub-agents versus directly exposing tools to a model.

Essential Job Functions and Responsibilities

  • Design the orchestration and abstraction layers of the central AI system that connect LLMs to tools, data, and sub-agents

  • Design, build, and operate MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers and set standards for how tools are defined, exposed, and versioned

  • Define tool-surface strategy: the optimal number of tools exposed to an LLM, the optimal number of APIs per MCP server, and how to keep tool surfaces coherent and discoverable

  • Establish when to use specialized sub-agents versus directly exposing tools to a model, and design the corresponding multi-agent patterns

  • Design retrieval (RAG) systems: chunking strategies, embedding models, vector stores, hybrid/keyword search, re-ranking, and context assembly

  • Define abstraction layers that decouple product teams from the underlying models, tools, and providers

  • Build routing, context-window management, and memory strategies for agentic workflows

  • Define evaluation for orchestration and retrieval quality (retrieval precision/recall, tool-selection accuracy, task success, latency, and cost)

  • Establish observability and tracing across multi-step agent and tool calls

  • Address safety, guardrails, authentication, and access control across tools and agents

  • Partner with product teams to onboard their capabilities as tools and agents into the central AI system

  • Mentor engineers and raise orchestration and retrieval maturity across teams

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Deep hands-on experience with LLM orchestration frameworks (e.g., LangGraph, LlamaIndex, Semantic Kernel, or equivalents) and agentic patterns

  • Direct experience building MCP servers and tool/function-calling integrations

  • Evidence-based opinions on the optimal number of tools to expose to an LLM and the optimal number of APIs per MCP server, and on overall tool-surface design

  • A clear, defensible point of view on specialized sub-agents versus direct tool exposure, and the tradeoffs of each

  • Deep experience with retrieval/RAG: chunking strategies, embeddings, vector databases, hybrid search, and re-ranking

  • Experience designing abstraction layers and platform APIs that many teams build on top of

  • Strong understanding of context-window management, prompt/context assembly, and cost/latency optimization

  • Experience with evaluation and observability for agentic and retrieval systems

  • Ability to set strategy and standards while remaining hands-on in code

  • Strong stakeholder collaboration and problem-solving skills

Education and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related discipline; advanced degree preferred

  • 12 or more years of experience in software/AI engineering, with hands-on experience building LLM orchestration, agents, and retrieval systems

The above statements describe the general nature and level of work performed in this role. Other duties may be assigned.

In this exciting position, the Multimedia Content Reviewer will be writing and reviewing linguistic content in a language which they have a native level proficiency to ensure the highest quality of accuracy for customers using the world's foremost multimedia platforms. With time the Multimedia Content Reviewer will become the cultural ambassador for their language market and will be expected to produce fully localized content and flag potential cultural issues with content types, wording and articulate suggestions to make all content appropriate and relevant for the target markets. 

The ideal candidate possesses a background in journalism or similar, has proven creative writing skills, and a keen attention to detail. In addition to that, we’re seeking candidates that are passionate about music, film and tech and have a knack for iOS and Mac OS devices.

MAIN DUTIES

Security teams already have plenty of tools that find problems. What they're missing is a safe way to fix them at scale without breaking production. Detection is nice. Correction is what makes you secure. That's why enterprise buyers take the meeting, and it's what you'll be selling.

As Regional Sales Director, you'll own new business, selling to CISOs and IT and security leaders who are tired of chasing alerts. You won't be starting from a blank page. About You

Do you have a passion for the healthcare and pharmaceutical industry?

Do you want to work across a mix of strategy consulting projects that draw from competitor, customer, medical and commercial insights?

Are you a highly motivated professional interested in being part of a dynamic team of self-starters, working with global healthcare and pharmaceutical clients across the full product life cycle?

If so, consider turning your expertise into a valuable career at Prescient. We welcome applications from life science professionals with project management or consulting experience within our growing Competitive Strategy practice.

About Our Competitive Strategy Practice

Prescient has four core practices: Commercial, Competitive Strategy, Medical and Value, Pricing and Access. We specialise in supporting our biopharma clients in making insightful strategic choices for their products and portfolios. Our offerings are designed to anticipate and respond to competitive risk across the product life cycle – from early pipeline through post launch – delivering timely insights and strategic implications that enable integrated decision making across competitive intelligence, marketing, and medical and commercial functions.

When you join this exciting venture, you will work with global healthcare and pharmaceutical clients across the full product life cycle, from discovery to loss of exclusivity, to help them unlock the full potential of their brands and portfolios.

About the Opportunity

You will be part of a fast-growing PE-backed business that allows high-performing employees to make an impact and contribute to growing the business. You will have the chance to channel your experience and know-how into supporting the development and commercialization of our clients’ assets and portfolios.

As an Engagement Manager, you will act as the day-to-day lead on small and mid-size projects or key workstreams within larger engagements. You will increasingly work through others, coaching and supporting Analysts and Consultants, making strong individual contributions and providing effective support to senior team members where needed.

You will be a core point of contact for clients, developing productive and enduring relationships and establishing yourself as a credible strategic advisor. You will help ensure projects are delivered effectively, efficiently and in line with Prescient’s high quality standards.

As most of your clients will be based in the US, the Engagement Manager position requires a good understanding of the evolving US biopharmaceutical market and trends.

Key Responsibilities

  • Reporting: Report to a Director, Associate Vice President or Vice President within the Competitive Strategy practice, ensuring clear communication on project progress, risks and resource needs
  • Project Execution and Management:
    • Lead the day-to-day management of competitive strategy and competitive intelligence engagements, ensuring high-quality deliverables and adherence to timelines and budgets
    • Structure and manage workstreams, guide junior team members and ensure that analytical approaches align with client objectives
  • Client Interaction and Service:
    • Build credibility by understanding client contexts, anticipating needs and delivering thoughtful, actionable insights
    • Support senior leaders in ensuring clients experience best-in-class service throughout the engagement life cycle
  • Account Development:
    • Proactively identify and qualify new business opportunities across existing accounts, shaping proposals and recommending strategic growth pathways to account leads
    • Take a leading role in deepening client relationships, regularly engaging senior stakeholders, articulating value and driving account expansion through consistent, high-impact delivery
  • Subject Matter and Therapeutic Area Expertise:
    • Develop and apply a strong understanding of relevant therapeutic areas, clinical development pathways, regulatory considerations and competitive environments
  • Serve as a knowledge resource to internal teams
    • People Leadership: Provide day-to-day coaching, feedback and oversight to junior team members to support their development and ensure high-quality contributions
  • Conference and External Engagement: Attend industry conferences or virtual events to gather competitive insights, deepen therapeutic knowledge, and build familiarity with key stakeholders and trends

Essential Skills and Experience

  • Experience in biopharma client services and consulting is required; CI experience is preferred
  • Strong results orientation with a proven track record of:
  • Managing day-to-day project execution, ensuring high-quality outputs and timely delivery
  • Structuring workstreams, managing junior team members and maintaining project momentum
  • Awareness of business development opportunities, with the ability to recognize potential areas for account growth, contribute to proposal development and support senior leaders in strengthening client relationships
  • A strong grounding in therapeutic areas, clinical development, product strategy and the competitive landscape; ability to quickly learn new disease areas and modalities
  • Emerging client management skills:
    • Confidence in interacting directly with clients to clarify needs, present findings and support ongoing engagement
    • Ability to build trust through credibility, preparedness and thoughtful communication
    • Growing capability to act as a strategic partner, including recognizing business development opportunities to add value or expand support within an account
  • Clear and confident communication skills, enabling effective interaction with clients and internal teams, and the ability to contribute meaningfully to strategic discussions with guidance from senior colleagues
  • Ability to connect details to strategic implications, synthesize complex information and communicate insights in a clear, structured manner
  • Willingness to “roll up your sleeves” to support analyses while helping elevate the team’s work
  • Ability to give and receive feedback constructively
  • Ability to navigate ambiguity, adapt to new situations, and rapidly acquire new therapeutic or methodological expertise
  • BA/BS required; an advanced degree in a life science discipline is preferred

What We Offer

  • A competitive package and remuneration linked to performance
  • A strong values-based culture grounded in collaboration, curiosity and excellence
  • Tailored career development based on your interests and aspirations – not a one-size-fits-all approach
  • A team of smart, supportive colleagues who invest in each other’s success
  • Leaders who are accessible, ambitious for the team and committed to mentorship
  • Opportunities to influence the business and help shape our growing Competitive Strategy practice
  • A flexible working schedule and recognition for outstanding contributions
  • A flat hierarchy that empowers you to take ownership and make an impact

About Prescient Healthcare Group

Prescient® is a pharma services firm specializing in dynamic decision support and product and portfolio strategy. We partner with our clients to turn science into value by helping them understand the potential of their molecules, shaping their strategic plans and allowing their decision making to be the biggest differentiating factor in the success of their products. When companies partner with Prescient, the molecules in their hands have a greater potential for success than the same science in the hands of their competitors.

Founded in 2007, Prescient is a global firm with a footprint in 10 cities across three continents. Our team of nearly 475 experts partners with 27 of the top 30 biopharmaceutical companies, the fastest-growing mid-caps and cutting-edge emerging biotechs, including some of the biggest and most innovative brands. More than 70% of our employees hold advanced life science degrees, and our teams deliver an impressive depth of therapeutic, clinical and commercial expertise.

All full-time employees also are eligible to participate in various benefit plans, including medical, dental, vision, life, disability insurance and 401K; in each case in accordance with the terms of the applicable plans.

Veeva Vault PromoMats is the industry-leading platform that life sciences companies rely on to manage the full lifecycle of promotional content, from Medical, Legal, and Regulatory (MLR) review and claims management to digital asset management and multichannel content distribution. We are looking for an experienced product manager to own and grow core PromoMats capabilities that make our customers' marketing, commercial, and medical affairs teams more efficient and productive.

In this role, you will own the product strategy and roadmap for key PromoMats capabilities, such as claims management, MLR review workflows, and digital asset management. You will work closely with Engineering, UX, and customers to identify high-impact problems, define requirements, and ship solutions that balance ease of use with the rigor demanded by a highly regulated industry.

  • Customer Discovery: Engage directly with brand, marketing operations, medical, and regulatory teams at life sciences companies to understand how they create, review, and distribute content, and translate those insights into prioritized product requirements
  • Measurement & Impact: Define and track the metrics that prove customer value, reduction in MLR review cycles, time to approval, claims auto-link rates, and feature adoption, and use them to guide the next set of investments
  • Feature Definition & Delivery: Write clear specifications and partner with Engineering, UX, and QA through design, build, and release to ship capabilities that meet the scalability and quality standards of the Veeva Vault platform
  • Compliance & Automation: Deliver capabilities that reduce manual effort across the content lifecycle, automated claims linking, reference substantiation, workflow configuration, content reuse, and AI-assisted content checks, while preserving the auditability regulated customers require
  • Cross-Product & Go-to-Market Alignment: Partner with product teams across Vault to deliver connected experiences, and enable Sales, Services, and Support with the positioning, demos, and documentation needed to bring releases to market

  • Communication: Ability to translate complex AI concepts into business value for non-technical stakeholders in Marketing, Legal, Medical, and Regulatory departments
  • Collaboration: Proven track record of working with UX and Engineering to build intuitive tools for complex workflows
  • Marketing Acumen: Experience in Marketing or Marketing Operations, or building products for marketing teams, with a working understanding of how brand strategy, campaign planning, and content production come together
  • Marketing Process Fluency: Familiarity with the methodologies brand teams run on, creative and campaign briefs, agency and studio workflows, brand guidelines and governance, modular content and content supply chain models, omnichannel planning, and launch readiness

  • Marketing Technology: Working knowledge of the martech stack brand teams use alongside PromoMats, DAM and content platforms (e.g., Adobe Experience Manager, Aprimo, Sitecore), marketing work management (e.g., Adobe Workfront, Asana, Monday), marketing automation and CRM (e.g., Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Marketo, Veeva CRM, Vault CRM), and campaign analytics tools

jobs.title: Lead Product Manager, Fan Experience
jobs.excerpt: SeatGeek believes live events are powerful experiences that unite humans.
jobs.description:
SeatGeek believes live events are powerful experiences that unite humans. With our technological savvy and fan-first attitude we’re simplifying and modernizing the ticketing industry.

By catering to both fans and rightsholders, we're powering a new, open entertainment ecosystem where fans have effortless access to experiences, and venues have seamless access to their audiences. Because everyone should expect more from ticketing.

Most fans don't start their ticket search on SeatGeek. They start with a conversation with ChatGPT, a Google search, an Instagram ad, a team's website, an email, or a link from a friend. What happens in the first few seconds after they land decides whether they find their tickets with us or go back to searching.

Today that journey spans many surface areas and responsible teams. We're looking for a Lead Product Manager to focus on the end to end experience, from the first touchpoint through landing and onto the event page, including fans who leave and come back. Once fans land, you'll also own the consistency of the features that follow them across every surface, such as price display and fee transparency, credits and incentives, notifications, saved and followed events, and our guarantee and trust signals. Fans meet these everywhere, yet no single team owns them.

This role doesn't have its own squad. You'll deliver through other teams' roadmaps. That means setting the strategy, making the case, and partnering closely with PMs, engineering and design leads, and marketers to turn a fragmented journey into one experience. If you're energized by impact through influence rather than direct ownership of a single surface, this role is for you.

What you'll do

  • Drive the vision, strategy and metrics for how fans get from marketing channels (paid search, paid social, SEO, affiliates, partner links, email, push) through landing and through checkout
  • Stay on top of how discovery is changing, including AI assistants, AI-driven search and social commerce, and bring those opportunities to the right teams
  • Optimize the strategy for landing experiences (performer, venue, category and campaign pages, plus app deep links), so what fans see matches the ad, email or search that brought them
  • Lead the charge for cross-cutting features fans meet after they land, such as price display, credits and incentives, notifications, saved and followed events, and trust signals
  • Set up automated quality checks that keep the experience consistent as teams ship, from checks that price display, trust signals and other shared features match across surfaces, to evals for AI-powered experiences and AI agents that continuously walk key fan journeys. Use them to catch broken experiences, regressions and drop-off spikes before fans feel them
  • Map the full journey, find where fans drop off between teams, and build the case for fixing those gaps with data, research and clear sizing of the opportunity
  • Dig into the data yourself: analyze funnel, channel and experiment results, monitor journey metrics for shifts, and turn what you find into clear recommendations for partner teams
  • Run continuous discovery on the shopping experience, including fan research, data deep dives and competitive teardowns, and turn what you learn into a steady pipeline of ideas and experiments for partner teams
  • Shape the roadmaps of our Product and Marketing Teams. Bring prioritized, well-scoped opportunities into planning and get them committed
  • Run regular working sessions with partner teams to keep journey work aligned, sequenced and moving
  • Work AI-native: prototype ideas with AI coding tools to win buy-in from partner teams, use AI to synthesize research and data at speed, and share the workflows that work so other PMs adopt them
  • Champion the fan journey across the company, celebrate wins, and mentor junior members of the product team

What you have

  • 8+ years of product management in consumer e-commerce, marketplaces or travel, including work on acquisition funnels, landing experiences or growth
  • A proven ability to get work prioritized and shipped by teams you don't manage
  • Working fluency in paid marketing, SEO, AI-driven discovery, and attribution
  • Strong experimentation, analytical and written communication skills
  • Experience with pricing, trust or design-system work that spans many surfaces, and strong attention to detail
  • Bonus: Experience using automation or AI tools to monitor product quality at scale
  • Bonus: live events or ticketing experience

Our stack

You absolutely do not need experience with all of these, but we thought you might be curious. Tools can be learned, so we care much more about your general engineering skill than knowledge of a particular language.

  • Languages: Python, Go, C#+.NET Core, Swift, Next.js, TypeScript
  • Client Platforms: iOS, Android, Web (Desktop/Mobile)
  • Technologies: OAuth2.0 & Identity Management, Payment Tokenization
  • Event-driven Technologies: RabbitMQ, Kafka
  • Datastores: Postgres, Redis, Memcache, Elasticsearch
  • Cloud: AWS
  • Version control: Git (Gitlab)

Perks

  • Equity stake
  • Discretionary annual bonus
  • Flexible work environment, allowing you to work as many days a week in the office as you’d like or 100% remotely
  • A WFH stipend to support your home office setup
  • Unlimited PTO
  • Up to 16 weeks of fully-paid family leave
  • 401(k) matching
  • Student loan matching program
  • Health, vision, dental, and life insurance
  • Up to $25k towards family building, reproductive health services and Gender-affirming care
  • $500 per year for wellness expenses
  • Subscriptions to Headspace (meditation), Headspace Care (therapy), and One Medical
  • $360 per quarter to spend on tickets to live events
  • Annual subscription to Spotify, Apple Music, or Amazon music

The salary range for this role is $152,000 - $220,000 USD. This role is equity eligible. In addition, you may receive a discretionary annual bonus based on individual and company performance. jobs.description:
About the Role

Global Safety and Security (GSS) protects our people, our sites, and the physical and logical systems that keep the business running. Our security and protection programs are never single-team efforts: one rollout can touch physical security operations, customer experiences, site readiness, hardware provisioning, networking, cloud infrastructure, identity, and the data platforms above them — spanning many countries, on timelines tied to leases, permits, and vendors.

About the Team

We are hiring a Staff Security Engineer to help design and deliver strategic and durable security services. You own the technical and architectural plan, strategic partner engagement with technology providers, the delivery sequence, the dependencies, and the program status leadership relies on. You are accountable for outcomes influencing teams that you don’t manage. You will collaborate with software engineers, third-party providers, physical security operations, project managers running site readiness and provisioning, and networking and cloud infrastructure partners, and you will keep managers, directors, and senior leaders informed.

Security Enablement Engineering delivers security paved paths and capabilities that address systemic security issues through well-designed customer experiences, easy-to-adopt and robust, well-architected security solutions, systematically reducing organizational risk.

You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…

  • Own the design of our physical security systems integration layer — such as access control (PACS) and video management (VMS) platforms, the APIs they expose, and the connectors that carry their data into our systems of record.
  • Own end-to-end design and delivery of multi-domain security services spanning physical security systems, hardware provisioning and site readiness, cloud and network infrastructure, identity and access management, key management, and the reporting/observability layers on top. You’ll bring expertise deploying security solutions at scale across many of these domains.
  • Partner with our software engineers from design through implementation, ensuring the right security outcomes are achieved. Propose and review architecture, design highly resilient, secure and scalable solutions, deliver proactive feedback to drive continuous improvement, hold the interface contracts, and support services in production ensuring operational excellence.
  • Own the cloud footprint of the security stack. The AWS services that host and scale these systems, the identity and network boundaries around them.
  • Own execution of complex and ambiguous security initiatives through detailed working-backwards plans. Start from the outcome and the date, then derive the dependency chain, critical path, owners, and the decisions that must land before each gate.
  • Look around corners. Surface and manage delivery risks before they escalate. Keep a risk register that’s well managed with an owner, a mitigation, and a delivery date.
  • Unblock, and escalate when unblocking requires it. Resolve most cross-team friction through direct collaboration. Escalate early, with a recommendation, and tradeoffs to leadership. Escalation is a deliberate tool, not a last resort.
  • Be the single source of truth on status. Concise written updates for senior leaders: what is on track, what is at risk, what changed, what decision we need. Manage stakeholder expectations from leadership to individual teams, apply strong problem solving and negotiation skills, and earn the trust of partners and teams.
  • Drive technical decisions to closure and operate through ambiguity. Frame the trade-offs, make recommendations on tooling (build/buy) and document what was decided and why.
  • Contribute to the vision, strategy, technical direction, and success metrics. Mentor engineers and program managers across GSS and partner teams. Review their plans, coach them on written status and risk framing, and help continually raise the operational and security bar. Develop shared goals with security partners, and identify solutions that optimize or automate manual, inefficient processes.

We’re excited about you because…

  • You have led multi-team, multi-quarter technical programs and owned the outcome across organizational boundaries.
  • You have a deep understanding of at least three security engineering domains and broad understanding across many: Identity and Access Management, Physical Security Systems, Security Operations, Detection and Response, DevSecOps, Security Architecture and Engineering, and Network Security.
  • You can read a network diagram, reason about a cloud deployment topology, understand hardware and firmware lifecycles, and hold a credible conversation with an infrastructure engineer about their constraints.
  • Global-scale software or cloud rollouts, including vendor-supplied platforms deployed across many sites and regions, with the integration and migration work that implies.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication — plans and status a director can act on and a senior engineer will not dismiss, and the range to convey security priorities and concepts to experts and non-experts alike.
  • Influence without authority, agility in re-planning when reality changes rather than defending the original plan, and comfort with physical-world constraints: sites, hardware, permits, and installers do not behave like pure software programs.
  • You have raised the bar for others without managing them — mentoring engineers and program managers, and improving plans and status through proactive feedback.
  • You have strong ownership, urgency, autonomy and drive. You are willing to roll up your sleeves and dive into the details to understand and drive your programs, and you focus on progress, not perfection.

Qualifications

Required

  • 6+ years in security or infrastructure engineering, including 4+ leading multi-team technical programs.
  • Bachelor of Science in Computer Science, Security Engineering, Information Systems, or equivalent years of experience in a related technical field
  • Expertise with cloud-based services and infrastructure (AWS, Google Cloud, etc.)
  • Hands-on depth with enterprise access control and video platforms (Lenel, Genetec, Milestone, or peers) and the APIs and integrations around them.
  • Project planning and execution skills that include JIRA experience, reviewing technical design documents, security controls, estimating, and scheduling.

Preferred

  • Physical security, access control, or safety-technology programs; a security or trust-and-safety organization; standing up program practice where none existed.
  • Proficiency in SQL data analysis, Python coding, and other automation tooling.
  • Experience with building Agentic workflows.

We expect this position to be filled by 12/15/2026

Compensation

The successful candidate’s starting pay will fall within the pay range listed below and is determined based on job-related factors including, but not limited to, skills, experience, qualifications, work location, and market conditions. Base salary is localized according to an employee’s work location. Ranges are market-dependent and may be modified in the future.

In addition to base salary, the compensation for this role includes opportunities for equity grants. Talk to your recruiter for more information.

DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits package to all regular employees, which includes a 401(k) plan with employer matching, 16 weeks of paid parental leave, wellness benefits, commuter benefits match, paid time off and paid sick leave in compliance with applicable laws (e.g. Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act). DoorDash also offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, 11 paid holidays, disability and basic life insurance, family-forming assistance, and a mental health program, among others.

To learn more about our benefits, visit our careers page here.

At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers.
