jobs.title: Senior Program Manager
jobs.excerpt: Points North is looking for a Senior Program Manager who is excited to support the way a growing, 60-person SaaS company gets its most important work done.
jobs.description:
Points North is looking for a Senior Program Manager who is excited to support the way a growing, 60-person SaaS company gets its most important work done. This is not a PMO role where you install a methodology and police it. It is a hands-on role at a company that has grown on the strength of good people and good instincts and now needs just enough structure to keep that working as we take on bigger things: major product launches, company-wide initiatives, and a brand-new product experiment that needs an owner.

You will report to the VP of Engineering, but you will serve with the whole company. Product and Engineering, then Sales, Customer Success, Client Support, Implementation, Operations, Managed Services, Finance, Marketing, and People and Culture. You will be evolving program and project governance from close to zero, which means you get to decide what good looks like here, and you get to live with the results.

If you are the kind of person who believes the best process is the one nobody notices because it just works, who has seen heavyweight frameworks slow good teams down and has no interest in importing one, and who is as comfortable owning a product backlog as you are running a cross-functional launch, we want to talk to you.

What You’ll Be Doing:

  • Enhance lightweight program and project governance for Product and Engineering, and then for the company. Collaboratively structure and then document how work gets proposed, prioritized, tracked, and finished. Build the minimum that gives leaders the visibility and teams the clarity they need, and then defend that minimum against the natural pull toward more.

  • Run our largest cross-functional initiatives end to end. Major product launches, operational improvement projects, and company-wide changes that touch every department. Own the plan, the dependencies, the risks, the communication, and the follow-through, so that the people doing the work know what they need to do and can focus on the work.

  • Support the adoption of AI tools across the company. Not a mandate from above, but a real program: find where AI tooling makes people measurably more effective, help teams try it, learn what works, and spread it. Use AI yourself as a force multiplier in how you plan, communicate, and analyze.

  • Be the Product Owner for an early-stage product experiment. We have one engineer dedicated to an early-stage internal tool that may have wider market opportunities. For at least the next six to twelve months, you will own the product side of that experiment: talk with internal and external stakeholders to vet which problems are worth solving, decide how to solve them and in what order, write clear requirements the engineer can build from, and build the evidence for whether there is a larger market. If it succeeds, we will hire a dedicated product manager to hand off to, and you will continue as our Senior Program Manager.

  • Make priorities visible and tradeoffs explicit. Help leadership see what is in flight, what is competing for the same people, and what it costs to say yes to something new. Bring data and a point of view and let the executives make the call with clear information.

  • Facilitate the Agile events and rituals that earn their keep. Planning, reviews, retrospectives, and the rhythms that keep teams aligned, tuned to what actually helps the team ship rather than what a framework prescribes.

  • Build the operating cadence for the company. Quarterly planning, status reporting that people actually read, decision logs, and the handful of templates that make the next project easier than the last one. Document it well enough that it runs without you in the room.

  • Partner with every function. Spend real time with Sales, Customer Success, Support, Implementation, Operations, Managed Services, Finance, Marketing, and People and Culture. Understand how each team works before suggesting how it could work better.

  • Close the loop. When an initiative finishes, find out whether it delivered what it promised based on the metrics and success criteria established at kickoff. Run honest retrospectives and share what you learn to improve how we run the next one.

  • Continuously learn and grow, in program management, in product thinking, and in how you help a company get better at getting things done.

What We Are Looking For:

  • A practical thinker who knows the goal is a company that executes well, not a governance model for its own sake.

  • A builder of just-enough process. Someone who has seen both ends of the spectrum, chaos and bureaucracy, and has a practiced instinct for the lightweight middle. You know that a process which is not followed is worse than no process at all.

  • A practitioner of real Agile software development. You have worked inside teams that actually ship this way, and you understand the principles well enough to adapt the practices to the team instead of forcing the team to fit the practices.

  • Someone with enough product instinct to own a product. You can sit with a customer, hear a problem underneath the request, decide what to build first, and write a requirement an engineer can act on without a meeting to decode it.

  • A strong communicator who can brief an executive in two minutes, run a working session with a sales or operations team, and write a status update that people read all the way to the end. You follow up on your commitments and your questions.

  • Someone who is enthusiastic about AI as an enabler, eager to experiment with AI-assisted tooling in your own work and to help others do the same, without abdicating judgment.

  • A collaborator who earns trust across departments by being useful, not by holding authority. People should want you in the room because things go better when you are there.

  • Someone who takes pride in enabling others and finds real satisfaction in a team finishing something big and knowing that your work under them made it easier.

Qualifications:

  • 10+ years of experience in program management, project management, product management, or a combination, with a track record of delivering large, cross-functional initiatives in a software company.
  • 10+ years of experience working in a SaaS company or small, fast-paced environment.

  • Hands-on experience with Agile software development as it is actually practiced by small, effective teams. Scrum or similar experience is a requirement.

  • Experience leading operational improvement or organizational change initiatives that spanned multiple departments.

  • Product management experience: customer discovery, requirements definition, backlog ownership, and prioritization. Experience validating a new product or market is a strong plus.

  • Experience building program or portfolio governance from an early stage, in a company that did not already have it.

  • Comfort with ambiguity and with being the person who creates clarity, rather than the person who waits for it.

  • Strong written communication. You have written plans, updates, and requirements that people read and acted on.

  • Fluency with modern collaboration and work-tracking tools (for example Azure DevOps, Jira, or similar, we use Azure DevOps)

  • Fluency with AI tools such as CoPilot and or Claude and a willingness to judiciously use AI tools as part of your daily work.

  • Bonus: Experience in a regulated industry, or with payroll, HRIS, or benefits data and the handling requirements that come with it.

  • Bonus: Experience leading an AI adoption or similar technology-enablement initiative.
  • ​​​​​​​Comfortable working primarily Central Time hours, and up to 15% travel annually for quarterly planning, team offsites, all-company meetings, and more, as needed.

At Points North, we believe that taking care of our team is the foundation of our success. That’s why we’ve created a benefits package designed to support you both personally and professionally: 

  • Health Insurance: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans are available to keep you and your family healthy. 

  • Retirement Savings: Invest in your future with employer-matching contributions to a SIMPLE Traditional and/or ROTH IRA plan. 

  • Time Off: Generous PTO, paid holidays, and Volunteer Time Off (VTO) are offered so that you can take time to recharge and give back to what matters to you. 

  • Growth Opportunities: Professional development is encouraged whether it be in training, certifications, or other opportunities to boost your career. 

  • Flexibility: Depending on the role, remote or hybrid arrangements may be made available to fit your lifestyle and business needs. 

For this position the base salary range is $135,000.00-$165,000 per year, plus additional annual bonus program eligibility. Final compensation determinations will reflect your unique experience, skills, and the responsibilities of the role. 

At Points North, you’ll find an energizing, ambitious and supportive workplace where your contributions make a real impact. Ready to join our team? Apply today to take the next step in your career!

jobs.title: Platform Security Engineer
jobs.excerpt: 🧡 CoverflexWork changed.  Pay didn’t. Coverflex exists to make compensation work for everyone.
jobs.description:
🧡 Coverflex

Work changed. Pay didn’t.

Coverflex exists to make compensation work for everyone.
Pay is still rigid, fragmented, and hard to feel.
We turn compensation into choice — one platform, one card, one app — for benefits, meal allowance, insurance and more.

Our platform is simple for HR and meaningful for employees.
We provide choice, smarter compensation tools and empowerment.

⚙️ TL;DR (The Essentials)

Role: Platform Security Engineer
Seniority Level: Senior
Type: Individual Contributor
Languages: English (main) / Portuguese / Spanish / Italian
Main Tools:AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform, GitHub Actions,Ubicloud, Datadog, CI/CD security scanning, identity and secrets management
Main Stack:Elixir/Phoenix, PostgreSQL, React Native (Expo)
Location: Remote (Europe only)
Compensation:

  • Base Salary:50.000€ to 67.000€ gross yearly

  • Bonus / Commissions: No

  • Equity: Yes – Stock Options under our Equity Incentive Plan

  • Benefits: All Coverflex benefits apply

  • Contract Type: Permanent

💥 Your Impact

Your role will play a major role in our success because…
→ We look after people's benefits and personal data in several countries, so trust is at the heart of what we do. As we grow, you'll make sure our security grows with us. You'll bring deep security expertise to DevX, the team that builds the platform and paved road for our engineers, and you'll make the secure path the easiest path for everyone.

You’ll know you’re successful when, after 90 days, you’ve…
->Shipped your first secure-by-default workflow for production operations, with access that's controlled, auditable and easy to use
->Shaped how we run security in our delivery pipeline: priorities, response targets and automation
->Led a resilience exercise that sharpened our recovery playbooks

How we’ll measure success:

  • Main KPI 1: More production operations running through secure, self-service and observable tooling

  • Main KPI 2: Security findings caught early in the delivery pipeline and resolved quickly, with automation doing the heavy lifting

  • Main KPI 3: Business continuity we can count on, with clear recovery targets that we test regularly

  • Secondary KPI 1: Edge protection that adapts to our applications and keeps the user experience smooth

  • Secondary KPI 2: Engineers adopt the security guardrails and are happy with them

⚡ Reality Check - What Makes This Role Hard

Let’s be real - here’s what makes this role challenging:

  • You're a platform engineer first.Security is your main focus, but you're a full member of DevX. You'll share the team's wider work: infrastructure, CI/CD, developer tooling and experience, observability and incident troubleshooting. Expect a real share of your time on work that isn't about security.

  • The challenge is to improve our security posture while improving developer experience, raising security awareness across engineering teams, and making the secure path the easiest path.

  • A big part of the work is delivering meaningful, production-grade improvements without slowing developer throughput or impacting platform users. This requires clear prioritisation, safe rollout patterns, and tight feedback loops so we can move quickly while minimising operational risk and unnecessary friction.

👤 You

Must-haves (evidence, not years)

  • Owned application or platform security in a production cloud environment, with clear examples of impact

  • Strong cloud security fundamentals: IAM and identity plumbing (SSO/OIDC), secrets management, and least privilege in practice

  • Strong platform engineering across infrastructure as code, CI/CD with security built in, and observability

  • Strong experience running Kubernetes in production, including workload security and access controls

  • Cloud networking and edge: VPC boundaries, DNS, TLS, load balancing, CDN and WAF tuning

  • Reliability in practice: SLOs, on-call, threat modelling, incident command, and postmortems

  • Backup, restore and disaster recovery designed and actually exercised

  • Treats the platform as a product: measures adoption and developer experience

  • Uses AI tooling to accelerate engineering work, and builds it into the platform (agents, MCP, assisted operations)

  • Reads and writes code well enough to fix problems, not just report them

  • Fluent English required

Nice-to-have

  • ISO 27001, SOC 2 or DORA experience

  • Fintech, payroll, or other regulated-data background

  • Detection engineering or SIEM experience

  • PostgreSQL operations and safe schema migrations

  • Elixir, or comfort picking up a functional language

  • Cloud cost awareness and FinOps practices

  • Certifications welcome, but practical evidence weighs more

🧬 Your DNA

  • Enabler, not a blocker:you make security the default through automation, paved-road patterns and self-service guardrails

  • Builder at heart:you'd rather ship the fix than file the report, and you work alongside engineers to raise the bar together

  • Pragmatic about risk:you weigh costs and benefits, explain trade-offs clearly, and prefer small, safe changes that add up

  • Written-first communicator:you write decisions down and share context early so others can move fast

  • Deeply curious:you dig into hard problems and incidents, then turn what you learn into tooling and better defaults

You’ll probably find this frustrating if…

  • You see security as a gate to guard rather than a path to pave

  • You prefer auditing and reporting to building and fixing things hands-on

  • You measure progress in policies written rather than in real improvements

  • You do your best work with a ready-made roadmap rather than shaping one yourself

👥 Manager & Team

Meet Your Manager

Hiring Manager: Rui Alves - Tech Lead, Platform Engineering
Location: Portugal
LinkedIn Profile:

Profile Snapshot:

  • Energy:Steady and low-ego. I try to keep things calm, especially when priorities shift or incidents happen.

  • Communication:Structured, transparent, and written-first when it helps. I document decisions, trade-offs, and next steps so alignment survives the meeting.

  • Feedback Style:Direct and kind. I give feedback early and specifically, and I expect the same in return.

How to work with me - in the Manager's own words:

Expect a collaborative environment with clear priorities and a bias for small, safe changes that compound. I’ll help remove blockers, protect focus, and make sure we’re shipping work that improves both security posture and developer experience. I value calm, ownership, and good written communication.

Your Team

You’ll work day-to-day with:

  • Tina,Platform Engineer,

  • Hugo,Platform Engineer,

Key Stakeholders:

  • Tiago Fernandes (CTO)

  • Bruno Oliveira (VP Engineering)

  • Luís Coelho (Quality Team Lead)

Team Rituals:

  • Daily standup

  • Weekly planning

  • Bi-weekly retrospective

💜 Access & Belonging (Equal Opportunity)

We hire for impact and potential, not pedigree.
We welcome applications from people with non-linear careers, career breaks, caregiving gaps, and those changing fields.

No discrimination on the basis of age, disability, gender identity/expression, marital or family status, pregnancy, neurodivergence, race/ethnicity, religion/belief, sexual orientation, or any other protected ground.

Assessment fairness:
We anchor on evidence of outcomes (what you shipped, moved, or influenced).
We actively de-bias by using structured rubrics, multiple assessors, and blind screening most of the time (we won’t know your name, gender, or personal info until the interview stage).

📬 Application Clarity

No cover letter required.

Apply with your LinkedIn or upload your CV.
You will be asked a few short, relevant questions.

Total candidate time investment: ~5–6 hours end-to-end.

🧩 Hiring Stages (What to Expect, Why & How Long)

1. CV / LinkedIn Screen — Signal check vs must-haves

• Done by People + Hiring Manager.

• You’ll hear from us within 7 business days.

2. Quick Interview (Intro Call) — Mutual fit & context • 20-30 min
With DevX. Covers role scope, salary, location, and timeline.

3. Deep Dive: Engineering Mindset — How you think about engineering• 45–60 min
With DevX and an Engineering Manager.Built around outcomes, decisions, trade-offs and collaboration, using examples from your own experience.

4. Deep Dive: Technical — How you design and build • 45-60 min
With a Staff or Architecture engineer.A technical conversation about platform, cloud and security design, and the reasoning behind your choices.

5. Technical Pairing challenge — How you work hands-on • ≤90 min
With two DevX engineers. A practical infrastructure-as-code / CI/CD exercise. We look at how you approach the problem, how you work with others, and how you balance security with developer experience.

6. Culture Interview — Walkthrough + Q&A • 20–30 min
You’ll get actionable feedback either way.

7. Final Conversation (CEO / C-Level) — Values, strategy, and your growth • 30–45 min

🤖 AI & Hiring Tools Transparency

We use a few tools to reduce bias and improve documentation, not to make hiring decisions.

  • Teamtailor anonymisation: profiles are reviewed without relying on names/personal identifiers.

  • Meeting recording tools (e.g., ): may be used to capture interviews so we can focus on the conversation.

  • LLM: may be used to turn interview notes/transcripts into clear, structured summaries.

Important: every application is reviewed by a human, and no decision or rejection is made by AI. If recording is used, we’ll be transparent and (where required) ask for consent.

⏱️ Speed & Communication

  • Decision: within 4 weeks of your application.

  • Updates: weekly if the process runs longer.

  • Scheduling:interviews between 10:00–16:00 CET (flexible across Europe).

  • Feedback:from the Deep Dive: Engineering Mindset stage onwards, you’ll always receive written or verbal feedback - what went well, and what to strengthen next time.

  • Volonté de participer au contrôle de la qualité de nos logiciels
  • Capacité à apprendre et à s'adapter rapidement aux nouvelles technologies
  • Capacité à gérer la pression et à accomplir des tâches dans un environnement rapide et exigeant
  • Contribuer à l'identification de tout problème lié à la documentation, aux procédures et au flux de travail, avec un retour d'information lors de la réunion hebdomadaire.

  • Vous avez une connaissance de HTML, CSS et JavaScript modernes (React, Angular)
  • Vous avez une connaissance des micro-services RESTful et des API REST.
  • Vous avez une bonne compréhension de Java Spring Framework (Asset)

  • Vous possédez d'excellentes aptitudes au travail d'équipe
  • Vous avez un excellent sens du détail, des compétences en résolution de problèmes et la capacité d'apprendre et d'appliquer rapidement de nouveaux concepts, principes et solutions.
  • Vous devez posséder d'excellentes aptitudes à la communication (verbale et écrite)
  • Expérience de travail dans un environnement Agile
  • Maîtrise des outils de développement et des techniques de débogage.

Sophos is a cybersecurity leader defending 600,000 organizations globally with an AI-driven platform and expert-led services. Sophos meets organizations wherever they are in their security maturity and grows with them to defeat cyberattacks. Its solutions combine machine learning, automation, and real-time threat intelligence with frontline human expertise from Sophos X-Ops to deliver advanced, 24/7 threat monitoring, detection, and response.
Sophos offers industry-leading managed detection and response (MDR) alongside a comprehensive portfolio of cybersecurity technologies — including endpoint, network, email, and cloud security, extended detection and response (XDR), identity threat detection and response (ITDR), and next-gen SIEM. Together with expert advisory services, these capabilities help organizations proactively reduce risk and respond faster, with the visibility and scalability needed to stay ahead of evolving threats.
Sophos goes to market with a global partner ecosystem, including Managed Service Providers (MSPs), Managed Security Service Providers (MSSPs), resellers and distributors, marketplace integrations, and cyber risk partners, giving organizations the flexibility to choose trusted relationships when securing their business. Sophos is headquartered in Oxford, U.K. More information is available at .

Role Summary

Sophos is seeking an experienced and motivated Senior Incident Response Consultant to join our Incident Response (IR) service. The Sophos IR team is an elite group of incident responders that are engaged by organizations worldwide to respond to and neutralize cyber threats. Specializing in industry-standard forensic tools and Sophos technologies, the team provides comprehensive investigations, response actions, remediation guidance, and root cause analysis to combat a wide range of cybersecurity incidents.

As a Senior Incident Response Consultant on the Sophos IR team, you will be responsible for spearheading incident response engagements for customers who have experienced a cybersecurity attack. In this role, you will lead a team of Incident Response Consultants, running customer-facing calls, providing detailed written updates via email, and determining the priorities of the investigation, delegating tasks accordingly to your team.

In this role, you will be accountable for ensuring that the appropriate actions have been taken by both your team and the customer to effectively neutralize the threat. Additionally, you will be tasked with conducting a thorough root cause analysis to determine the origin of the incident, including identifying whether any data exfiltration occurred, provided the necessary evidence is available.

At the culmination of each engagement, you will be responsible for producing an executive summary-style report, which will include a timeline of key events mapped to the MITRE ATT&CK framework. This comprehensive report will serve as a valuable resource for stakeholders, highlighting the steps taken to combat the cybersecurity incident and provide remediation guidance.

The ideal candidate for this role will possess extensive experience leading incident response efforts, a deep understanding of cybersecurity threats and mitigation strategies, and the ability to communicate complex technical information to executive-level stakeholders in a clear and concise manner.

  • Conduct multiple Rapid Response incidents concurrently

  • Continuously learning and staying informed of the changing threat landscape
  • Proven track record of successful neutralization and remediation of ransomware threats
  • Excellent understanding of the Incident Response process
  • Excellent understanding of cyber risks and able to qualify them to customers
  • Excellent oral communication skills
  • Strong written communication skills
  • Ability to manage time effectively
  • Able to delegate and prioritize tasks across multiple incidents
  • Able to excel under stressful circumstances
  • Occasionally willing to begin work early and/or stay late when warranted for customer engagements
  • Strong grasp of the MITRE ATT&CK framework
  • Enjoy mentoring and assisting in the development of junior analysts
  • A team-player attitude with a willingness to share knowledge
